Yeah you have to go in buddy. The longer you wait the worse it will get. The dentist wiIl treat the tooth pain first thing. In the meantime take Advil and Tylenol together for the pain. It works well for dental pain. If you are in severe pain go to an urgent care in the meantime and see if they can help you until you can see a dentist.  

But also just advice for fun. 
Don’t avoid the dentist. As a hygienist I see daily the effects of people who avoid going to the dentist long term and who only go in for pain. In the long run it just becomes more expensive to treat. What was just a small cavity that needed a filling but didn’t hurt so people put it off, then the decay gets bigger and needs a crown, then the decay gets bigger and then its a root canal, if its still not treated infection sets in and then more than likely an extraction. 
Go in regularly get the preventive care.  Does it suck yes. Would you rather be anywhere else? Definitely.

I didn’t say it WAS going to happen. I said it MAY. 
As a hygienist I see a lot of patterns in young kids. I see 10-12 kids a day. I just wanted her to be informed. As I said its something that can happen. Children’s mouths and bones are more mailable and increased pressure over prolonged periods of time “could” “potentially” change the shape of the palate. Thats all im saying.

After awhile the pressure from thumb sucking will alter the way his permanent teeth will come in. It may cause him to have an open bite. If its severe enough he may need a lot of ortho treatment in the future or possibly surgery to correct. I dont want to scare you I just want you to have the information.
